headline: Substitute Ibrahim's goal leads Bangladesh to 1-0 win over Bhutan
summary: Mohammad Ibrahim scored the decisive goal in the 69th minute, securing a winning start for Bangladesh in their SAFF Championship opener.
details: Bangladesh secured a 1-0 victory over Bhutan in their SAFF Championship opener at the National Stadium on Thursday.
Substitute Mohammad Ibrahim scored the decisive goal in the 69th minute, just a few minutes after coming on for makeshift striker Bishwanath Ghosh.
Head coach Thomas Dooley had surprised many by deploying centre-back Bishwanath as the lone striker for the first 65 minutes.
Dooley admitted he did not expect Ibrahim to score, stating he brought him on primarily to hold the ball and set up other players.
The coach praised Bishwanath's energy and work rate up front, noting that the is not shy of going where it hurts to help the team.
Ibrahim's goal is a reward for his recent form, having recently scored a decisive goal for Fortis FC against Kyrgyzstan's Muras United.
Bangladesh is now aiming to reclaim the title they last won in 2003.
caption:
A surprise tactical move and a super-sub's clinical finish! Bangladesh beats Bhutan 1-0.

Bangladesh secured a 1-0 victory over Bhutan in their SAFF Championship opener at the National Stadium on Thursday.

Substitute Mohammad Ibrahim scored the decisive goal in the 69th minute, just a few minutes after coming on for makeshift striker Bishwanath Ghosh.

Head coach Thomas Dooley had surprised many by deploying centre-back Bishwanath as the lone striker for the first 65 minutes.

Dooley admitted he did not expect Ibrahim to score, stating he brought him on primarily to hold the ball and set up other players.

The coach praised Bishwanath's energy and work rate up front, noting that the is not shy of going where it hurts to help the team.

Ibrahim's goal is a reward for his recent form, having recently scored a decisive goal for Fortis FC against Kyrgyzstan's Muras United.

Bangladesh is now aiming to reclaim the title they last won in 2003.

headline_marked: Two DGFI members [[dismissed and jailed]] in extortion case
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed in extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were sentenced to one year in prison after a court martial for attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested in October after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.
The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to buy a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted by four people.
The victim had handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He later managed to escape and inform a police patrol vehicle near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.
After their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law.
The court martial proceedings proved the allegations against them, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been dismissed and jailed for one year after attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested in October after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to buy a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted by four people.

The victim had handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He later managed to escape and inform a police patrol vehicle near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.

After their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law.

The court martial proceedings proved the allegations against them, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.
